summary.verdict: CONDITION-ROBUST essentiality adds a target-QUALITY axis (environment/host independence). Across 6 media (glc_aer, glyc_aer, ac_aer, succ_aer, glc_anaer, glc_supplemented): 116 genes are essential in EVERY condition (maximally robust). H1 (validity): condition-robust essentials are enriched for EXPERIMENTAL (PEC) essentiality at 0.793 vs 0.477 for the FULL essential set (+0.316) -> condition-robustness is a STRONG, validated quality filter that tracks true core-essentiality (CONFIRMED); the medium-supplemented condition alone drops essentials 196->117 (biosynthesis genes become dispensable when nutrients are provided — exactly the host-bypass risk this captures). H2 (target quality): 8/9 nominated broad-spectrum targets are condition-robust (essential regardless of nutrient environment -> environment-independent, higher-quality interventions); the rest are medium-specific (biosynthesis genes bypassable when the host supplies the nutrient -> weaker as monotherapy). This directly upgrades target selection toward 'best INTERVENTION' and quantifies the medium-dependence caveat that dogged the whole essentiality arc. HONEST SCOPE: iML1515/E. coli in-silico; media are FBA approximations of environments, NOT a real host; PEC is rich-medium experimental truth; hypotheses; not wet-lab.
